Accordion.description: The Accordion component lets users show and hide sections of related content on a page. It includes several complementary utility components: Accordion (wrapper), AccordionSummary (header), AccordionDetails (content), and AccordionActions (optional buttons).

Alert.description: Alerts display brief messages for the user without interrupting their use of the app. They give users brief and potentially time-sensitive information in an unobtrusive manner.

AppBar.description: The App Bar displays information and actions relating to the current screen. It provides content and actions related to the current screen and can transform into a contextual action bar or be used as a navbar.

Autocomplete.description: The autocomplete is a normal text input enhanced by a panel of suggested options. It's useful for setting the value of a single-line textbox in scenarios where the value must be chosen from a predefined set or where suggesting possible values is advantageous.

Avatar.description: Avatars are found throughout material design with uses in everything from tables to dialog menus. They can contain images, letters, or icons representing a person or object.

Backdrop.description: The Backdrop component narrows the user's focus to a particular element on the screen. It signals a state change within the application and can be used for creating loaders, dialogs, and more. In its simplest form, it adds a dimmed layer over your application.

Badge.description: Badge generates a small badge to the top-right of its children. It can contain text or numbers and is used to indicate notifications, counts, or status.

BottomNavigation.description: The Bottom Navigation bar allows movement between primary destinations in an app. Bottom navigation bars display three to five destinations at the bottom of a screen, each represented by an icon and optional text label.

Box.description: The Box component is a generic, theme-aware container with access to CSS utilities from MUI System. It serves as a wrapper component for most of the CSS utility needs and provides a convenient way to rapidly prototype new features.

Breadcrumbs.description: A breadcrumbs is a list of links that help visualize a page's location within a site's hierarchical structure. It allows navigation up to any of the ancestors and helps users understand where they are in the site hierarchy.

Button.description: Buttons allow users to take actions, and make choices, with a single tap. They communicate actions that users can take and are typically placed throughout your UI, in places like modal windows, forms, cards, and toolbars.

ButtonGroup.description: The ButtonGroup component can be used to group related buttons. The buttons need to be immediate children and can be grouped by wrapping them with the ButtonGroup component.

Card.description: Cards contain content and actions about a single subject. They are surfaces that display content and actions on a single topic.

Checkbox.description: Checkboxes allow users to select one or more items from a set. They can be used to turn an option on or off. If you have multiple options appearing in a list, you can preserve space by using checkboxes instead of on/off switches.

Chip.description: Chips are compact elements that represent an input, attribute, or action. They allow users to enter information, make selections, filter content, or trigger actions.

ClickAwayListener.description: The Click-Away Listener component detects when a click event happens outside of its child element. This is useful for components like Popper which should close when the user clicks anywhere else in the document.

Container.description: The Container component is the most basic layout element that centers your content horizontally. It's a fundamental building block for creating responsive layouts.

CssBaseline.description: The CssBaseline component helps to kickstart an elegant, consistent, and simple baseline to build upon. It provides a global reset similar to normalize.css and applies better page-wide defaults.

Dialog.description: Dialogs inform users about a task and can contain critical information, require decisions, or involve multiple tasks. A Dialog is a type of modal window that appears in front of app content to provide critical information or ask for a decision.

Divider.description: The Divider component provides a thin, unobtrusive line for grouping elements to reinforce visual hierarchy. It renders as a dark gray horizontal rule by default.

Drawer.description: The navigation drawers (or "sidebars") provide ergonomic access to destinations in a site or app functionality such as switching accounts. They can either be permanently on-screen or controlled by a navigation menu icon.

FloatingActionButton.description: A Floating Action Button (FAB) performs the primary, or most common, action on a screen. It appears in front of all screen content, typically as a circular shape with an icon in its center.

Grid.description: The responsive layout grid adapts to screen size and orientation, ensuring consistency across layouts. It's based on a 12-column grid layout and uses CSS Flexible Box module for high flexibility.

GridLegacy.description: The legacy Grid component from Material Design responsive layout system. It uses CSS Flexible Box module and is based on a 12-column grid layout. Note: This component is deprecated and Grid v2 should be used instead.

ImageList.description: The Image List displays a collection of images in an organized grid. Image lists represent a collection of items in a repeated pattern and help improve the visual comprehension of the content they hold.

Link.description: The Link component allows you to easily customize anchor elements with your theme colors and typography styles. It's built on top of the Typography component.

List.description: Lists are continuous, vertical indexes of text or images. They are a continuous group of text or images composed of items containing primary and supplemental actions, which are represented by icons and text.

Masonry.description: Masonry lays out contents of varying dimensions as blocks of the same width and different height with configurable gaps. It maintains a list of content blocks with consistent width but different height, ordered by row.

Menu.description: Menus display a list of choices on temporary surfaces. A menu displays a list of choices on a temporary surface that appears when the user interacts with a button or other control.

Modal.description: The modal component provides a solid foundation for creating dialogs, popovers, lightboxes, or whatever else. It renders its children node in front of a backdrop component and manages modal stacking, creates a backdrop, disables scrolling, and properly manages focus.

NoSsr.description: The No-SSR component defers the rendering of children components from the server to the client. This can improve time to first paint, reduce rendering time on the server, or turn on service degradation when server load is too heavy.

NumberField.description: A React component for capturing numeric input from users. It's composed of a Base UI Number Field and styled to align with Material UI specs. Provides increment and decrement buttons for easy value adjustment.

Pagination.description: The Pagination component enables the user to select a specific page from a range of pages. It provides navigation controls to move between pages of content.

Paper.description: In Material Design, surface components and shadow styles are heavily influenced by their real-world physical counterparts. Material UI provides a Paper component that renders as an elevated surface with shadow effects.

Popover.description: A Popover can be used to display some content on top of another. It's built on top of the Modal component, with scroll and click away blocked.

Popper.description: A Popper can be used to display some content on top of another. It's an alternative to react-popper that aims for simplicity and relies on Popper.js for perfect positioning. The scroll isn't blocked and clicking away does not hide the component.

Portal.description: The Portal component lets you render its children into a DOM node that exists outside of the Portal's own DOM hierarchy. It's built around React's createPortal API and is useful when you need the child element to visually break out of its container.

Progress.description: Progress indicators inform users about the status of ongoing processes. Circular and Linear progress components express either determinate (known duration) or indeterminate (unknown duration) wait times.

RadioButton.description: Radio buttons allow users to select one option from a set. Use radio buttons when the user needs to see all available options. If available options can be collapsed, consider using a Select component because it uses less space.

Rating.description: Ratings provide insight regarding others' opinions and experiences, and can allow the user to submit a rating of their own.

Select.description: Select components are used for collecting user provided information from a list of options. They allow users to select one item from a dropdown list.

Skeleton.description: Display a placeholder preview of your content before the data gets loaded to reduce load-time frustration. Skeletons make it feel like things are happening immediately.

Slider.description: Sliders allow users to make selections from a range of values. They reflect a range of values along a bar, from which users may select a single value. They are ideal for adjusting settings such as volume, brightness, or applying image filters.

Snackbar.description: Snackbars (also known as toasts) are used for brief notifications of processes that have been or will be performed. They appear temporarily and float above the UI to provide users with non-critical updates.

SpeedDial.description: When pressed, a floating action button can display three to six related actions in the form of a Speed Dial. It's used for displaying related actions.

Stack.description: Stack is a container component for arranging elements vertically or horizontally. It manages the layout and spacing between immediate children along the vertical or horizontal axis.

Stepper.description: Steppers convey progress through numbered steps. They display progress through a sequence of logical and numbered steps and may also be used for navigation.

Switch.description: Switches toggle the state of a single setting on or off. They are the preferred way to adjust settings on mobile. The option that the switch controls, as well as the state it's in, should be made clear from the corresponding inline label.

Table.description: Tables display sets of data in a way that's easy to scan, so users can look for patterns and insights. They can be fully customized and can include visualization, navigation, and tools to query data.

Tabs.description: Tabs make it easy to explore and switch between different views. They organize and allow navigation between groups of content that are related and at the same level of hierarchy.

TextareaAutosize.description: The Textarea Autosize component automatically adjusts its height to match the length of the content within. It replaces the native textarea HTML element and responds to keyboard inputs and window resizing events.

TextField.description: Text Fields let users enter and edit text. They are used in forms to allow users to input text, numbers, and other data. The TextField wrapper component is a complete form control including a label, input, and help text.

ToggleButton.description: A Toggle Button can be used to group related options. Groups of related Toggle buttons should share a common container. The ToggleButtonGroup controls the selected state of its child buttons.

Tooltip.description: Tooltips display informative text when users hover over, focus on, or tap an element. They display a text label identifying an element, such as a description of its function.

TransferList.description: A Transfer List (or shuttle) enables the user to move one or more list items between lists. It's useful for selecting and organizing items between two columns.

Typography.description: Use typography to present your design and content as clearly and efficiently as possible. The Typography component makes it easy to apply a default set of font weights and sizes in your application following the Material Design typographic scale.
